faqs.q: How do I convert my Victoria Police salary from hourly to annual?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, an hourly rate of $40 gives $40 × 38 × 52 = $79,040 gross per year. If you receive casual loading (25% on top), the rate becomes $50 per hour, resulting in $98,800 annually. Remember that super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12%.

faqs.q: Does the Victoria Police salary include casual loading?
faqs.a: Victoria Police officers are typically employed as permanent full-time or part-time staff, not casuals, so casual loading generally does not apply. However, if you are a casual employee in a policing support role, you may be entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. Always check your employment type and award.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on a Victoria Police salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the super guarantee rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). For a full-time Victoria Police salary of $106,137, your employer would contribute an additional $12,736.44 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This is separate from your gross pay and is not subject to income tax until withdrawal.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Victoria Police Salary: Hourly to Annual

When you're evaluating a **Victoria Police salary** offer or comparing it to other roles, understanding how to convert an hourly rate to an annual figure is essential. This guide walks you through the formula, explains casual loading and superannuation, and shows how tax affects your take-home pay.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a standard full-time position, we assume 38 hours per week as per the Fair Work Ombudsman's definition. For example, if your **Victoria Police salary** is advertised at $45 per hour, your annual gross would be $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920.

If you work part-time or irregular hours, adjust the weekly hours accordingly. The formula assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. If you're a casual in a policing support role, your effective hourly rate becomes base × 1.25. For instance, a base rate of $30 becomes $37.50 per hour. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** into the timesheet; instead, use the checkbox to add it.

Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12% (super guarantee rate from 1 July 2026). It does not reduce your gross pay; it's an additional contribution your employer makes. For a **Victoria Police salary** of $88,920, your employer would add $10,670.40 in super, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Estimates

To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $45/hour example: weekly = $45 × 38 = $1,710; fortnightly = $3,420. This helps when budgeting or comparing to award rates.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees get $33.05 per hour including 25% loading. Most **Victoria Police salary** levels are above these minimums, as police roles are covered by specific awards or enterprise agreements. The figures here are averages, not your specific job median.

### Tax and Medicare

Using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed. For a **Victoria Police salary** of $88,920, tax would be approximately $18,967 plus Medicare $1,778, leaving about $68,175 after tax (excluding HELP or surcharges).

### Average Earnings Context

According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult ordinary time weekly earnings in Victoria were $2,041.10 in May 2026. That's an average across all industries, not a median for Victoria Police. Your actual **Victoria Police salary** may differ based on rank, experience, and allowances.

### Using the Timesheet

Our [timesheet](/) lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It calculates annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures, plus estimated tax and super. Remember the disclaimer: this is an estimate, not a determination of your pay.

For more detailed pay guides, visit our [pay guides](/blog) page. You can also explore [reference tables](/data) for award rates and [average pay](/topics/average-pay) data.

### Key Takeaways

- Annual gross = hourly × 38 × 52 (for full-time)
- Casual loading adds 25% on top; super adds 12% on top
- Tax uses 2026–27 rates; Medicare is 2%
- The **Victoria Police salary** average is $2,041.10 per week (full-time ordinary time in Victoria), but your specific rate depends on your role
- Always check your award or enterprise agreement for exact conditions
